title: Roger Johnson's death and George Girard
summary: He remembers drummer Roger Johnson dying young, and that he gave trumpeter George Girard his first Bourbon Street job.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: How old was Roger Johnson when he died? He was quite young.
Oh yeah. Roger, well he was in his forties, I'd say about 46.

I remember the day that happened I was talking about him with Bob Coquille and Paul Crawford. We were over at the French market having coffee, and we were talking about how Roger was just working too hard.
He was an excellent drummer too, but he worked at it. When he played he worked, boy. He tried, you know.
Yeah. I think he was working days too, wasn't he?
No, I don't think. Not then when he knew he was going to die. He was supposed to give up smoking, give up drinking, and he said, well you've got to go and die once, and so he did.
It's funny, we were talking about him and we didn't know he'd, uh, we didn't know he'd passed. We were talking about how I guess this is he was dying. That was a fantastic job.

He had worked with me before Nick's, I mean before our famous dog. He worked with me at the Moulin Rouge, which is now Ciro's. Oh yeah. Playing shows in there for a while in the Latin Quarter where I first used George to ride, gave George his first job on Bourbon Street. He never did forget the fact. I didn't know that. George offered me a job every time, the whole time he was in the famous door, every time he'd see me he'd say, when are you going to come to work with me?
He was a fine boy, a lot of talent. Fantastic lip.
How many could get those notes?
Well he was a fine showman, good entertainer. Was he a reader much? Not too much, no.
I think he played with some big bands.

Yeah but you learn the parts more or less, you learn the parts by memory or you know, you just, what is it called, woodshed them until you know the things and it's just a reputation, playing the same thing over, you see.
